aAbout: VesselFinder tracks ships worldwide through 7,000+ terrestrial AIS data sources, with satellite AIS layered on top for open-ocean coverage (it says 90% of satellite positions arrive within an hour). The site pairs positions with vessel photos, port data, weather overlays and a distance tool. Its plans are published in plain dollars and undercut the market leader at every tier, and its subscriptions do not renew automatically. API access and historical data are sold separately.
aStrengths: VesselFinder's edge is honest, budget maritime tracking: affordable satellite AIS covering the open oceans where terrestrial receivers can't reach, a practical single-ship satellite option for occasional needs, vessel photos and particulars, and plans that undercut the big rivals at every level — Basic is $12 for a whole year. For port agents, cargo superintendents and individual surveyors who need affordable fleet watching, it is the value play in ship tracking.
bAbout: ShipFinder at shipfinder.com is a web-only satellite + terrestrial AIS platform associated with Elane. It combines land-based AIS with satellite AIS for open-ocean coverage, and pairs live positions with historical tracks and playback, port calls, route prediction and ETAs, fleet management and vessel event alerts, plus an AIS API and an Enterprise tier. There is no app to download — its Help Center says to use it in a mobile browser, with the account and data syncing to the desktop version. Its own pages publish no vessel or port count.
bStrengths: ShipFinder's edge is satellite-first tracking at a simple, published price: satellite AIS starts on the free plan (1 vessel) rather than at a top tier, Professional unlocks unlimited satellite AIS for $99/month, and exports, nautical charts, route prediction and ETA, density heatmaps and vessel alerts are listed at every level. There is nothing to install — the whole platform runs in a browser, on desktop or mobile.
betterAnswer: VesselFinder is better for a cheap start and native apps — its Basic plan is $12 for a year and its subscriptions never renew automatically. ShipFinder is better once satellite coverage matters — satellite AIS starts free, and its Professional plan pairs unlimited satellite AIS with 6 months of history for $99/month. Casual viewers checking one ship are served by either free tier; the paid decision is really about fleet size and how much history you need.

faqs.q: Are there two different products called Ship Finder?

faqs.a: Free (10 ships, 1-day history), Basic $4/month or $12/year (20 ships, 3-day history), Premium $34/month or $179/year (500 ships, 7-day history) and Satellite $139/month or $1,399/year (2,000 ships, 90-day history, satellite AIS). Prices were checked against VesselFinder's subscription page in October 2026, exclude VAT, and subscriptions do not renew automatically.

ShipFinder at shipfinder.com is free at $0 (satellite AIS for 1 vessel, 3-day history, fleet of 10). Standard is $29/month or $290/year (5 satellite vessels, fleet of 20) and Professional is $99/month or $990/year (unlimited satellite AIS, 6-month history, fleet of 100). Enterprise is contact-only.

Both sell it, but at different points in the range. VesselFinder reserves satellite AIS for its Satellite plan ($139/month or $1,399/year, unlimited fleet in that plan, 90-day history) and says 90% of satellite positions arrive within an hour. ShipFinder includes satellite AIS at every level — 1 vessel free, 5 on Standard and unlimited on Professional at $99/month.
faqs.q: Which is cheaper for satellite AIS coverage?

Standard is where its own pages conflict: the pricing page says 14 days of history, while its Help Center says 7 days — so treat Standard history as 7–14 days. Enterprise is listed with 10+ years of historical vessel data.

seoDescription: VesselFinder vs ShipFinder (shipfinder.com) compared: AIS coverage, satellite tracking, fleet sizes, history and full 2026 pricing — the budget tracker vs the satellite-first challenger, plus a free third option.
seoTitle: VesselFinder vs ShipFinder (2026): Budget Tracking or Satellite Value?
verdictA: Choose VesselFinder if you want the cheapest credible start — a $12-a-year Basic plan, native apps and subscriptions that never renew behind your back — and your fleet is mostly in terrestrial coverage, with one satellite plan when you need the oceans.
verdictB: Choose ShipFinder if satellite coverage is the point — you want a free satellite-tracked vessel to start, unlimited satellite AIS with 6 months of history at $99/month, and a browser-only tool with no app to install.
verdictLine: VesselFinder is the budget play — the cheapest plans in ship tracking, honest non-renewing subscriptions and native apps. ShipFinder is the satellite play — satellite AIS from the free tier up, at two simple published prices. The first starts cheaper; the second goes offshore sooner.
worldEye: For casual watching, WorldEye shows live ships free on a 3D globe — no registration at all — in the same view as live flights, satellites, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras across 109 countries. It has neither VesselFinder's satellite plans nor ShipFinder's satellite-AIS plans or fleet-management features; it's the free, everything-at-once picture. An optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds.
